title: India–Denmark Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation in MSME Development, Innovation & Intellectual Property
subtitle: 4th Joint Working Group Meeting held in Copenhagen between Ministry of MSME, Government of India and the Danish Patent and Trademark Office (DKPTO)
body_text:
The 4th Meeting of the India–Denmark Joint Working Group (JWG) between the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, and the Danish Patent and Trademark Office (DKPTO) was held in Copenhagen, Denmark, from 24 to 28 August 2026, to strengthen bilateral cooperation in MSME development, innovation and intellectual property (IP).
The meeting provided a platform for India and Denmark to exchange perspectives on their respective MSME and innovation ecosystems and to explore opportunities for greater institutional cooperation. Discussions covered areas including technology adoption, innovation, intellectual property, technology commercialisation, entrepreneurship and cluster-based MSME development.
The Indian delegation was led by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME; Md. Salik Parwaiz, Director; Ms. Bhagya Jagadiswaran, Assistant Director; and Ms. Swapna Vanamala, Faculty Member, National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme). The Embassy of India in Copenhagen was represented by Mr. Manish Prabhat, Ambassador of India to the Kingdom of Denmark, and Mr. Ashish Arya, Counsellor. The Danish delegation comprised Ms. Maria Skou, Deputy Director General, DKPTO; Mr. Mattias Dinnetz, Senior Advisor, International Cooperation, DKPTO; and Ms. Louise Boisen, Counsellor, Intellectual Property Rights, Royal Danish Embassy, New Delhi.
Key Takeaways & Engagements
As part of the programme, the Indian delegation visited Aarhus University Innovation “Kitchen” and Agro Food Park to gain insights into Denmark’s innovation support and business cluster ecosystems. The engagements facilitated an exchange of experiences on mentoring, start-up support, industry–academia linkages and cluster-based approaches for supporting entrepreneurs and MSMEs.
The delegation also engaged with the Danish Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs to exchange views on business development, innovation and the SME ecosystem in Denmark.
The delegation, led by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, also participated in the Nordic–India Startup Summit 2026 by TechBBQ, a leading Nordic start-up event, which provided an opportunity to interact with stakeholders from the Nordic start-up and innovation ecosystem and share perspectives on India’s MSME sector.
The concluding JWG discussions reviewed the outcomes of previous engagements and deliberated upon priorities for future collaboration and opportunities to expand cooperation under the existing JWG framework. Ambassador of India to Denmark, Mr. Manish Prabhat, appreciated the successful functioning of the JWG mechanism and the deepening of India–Denmark cooperation. He reaffirmed support for continued engagement under the JWG framework and encouraged exploration of new and complementary areas of cooperation.
The meeting underscored the shared commitment of India and Denmark to promoting innovation and IP-led growth of MSMEs, while strengthening knowledge exchange, institutional linkages and opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation.

enrichment.summary: The 4th India–Denmark Joint Working Group meeting was held in Copenhagen from 24-28 August 2026 between India's Ministry of MSME and the Danish Patent and Trademark Office (DKPTO) to deepen bilateral cooperation on MSME development, innovation and intellectual property. The Indian delegation, led by Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner Dr. Rajneesh, visited Danish innovation hubs, met the Danish Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs, and participated in the Nordic-India Startup Summit 2026. Discussions covered technology adoption, IP, cluster-based MSME development and future areas of collaboration under the JWG framework.
enrichment.context:
This is a routine bilateral engagement under an existing institutional mechanism (the JWG has met four times) between India's MSME ministry and Denmark's patent office, focused on soft cooperation areas like knowledge exchange, cluster development, and IP awareness rather than any binding agreement, funding commitment, or policy announcement. Such JWGs are common instruments of India's economic diplomacy, used to facilitate exposure visits, exchange of best practices, and networking for officials and institutions like ni-msme, but they typically do not produce examinable policy outcomes.

MSMEs are significant to India's economy (contributing significantly to GDP, employment and exports), and government engagement with foreign counterparts on innovation ecosystems and cluster-based development ties into India's broader push for MSME competitiveness and IP-led growth. However, this specific release documents a diplomatic/administrative visit and exchange of views without new schemes, statistics, or policy decisions.
